title: Unstable image IDs when using the Docker-compatible API with labels
body:
### Issue Description

Several identical build requests with labels using the Docker compatible API don't produce identical image IDs.
IDs are stable when using the CLI though.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

The following MRE builds the same image 6 times through the Docker compatible API, with 4 labels, then 6 times with the podman CLI, and prints the image ID of each build.

```shell
#!/bin/sh
set -e
SOCK=${SOCK:-$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podman/podman.sock}
dir=$(mktemp -d)
printf 'FROM scratch\nENV FOO=bar\n' > "$dir/Dockerfile"
tar -C "$dir" -cf "$dir/context.tar" Dockerfile
labels=$(printf '%s' '{"a":"1","b":"2","c":"3","d":"4"}' | jq -sRr @uri)

echo "API:"
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
  curl -sf --unix-socket "$SOCK" -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-tar' \
    --data-binary @"$dir/context.tar" \
    "http://d/v1.41/build?t=label-repro-api&labels=$labels" > /dev/null
  podman image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' label-repro-api
done

echo "CLI:"
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
  podman build -q -t label-repro-cli --label a=1 --label b=2 --label c=3 --label d=4 "$dir" > /dev/null
  podman image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' label-repro-cli
done

rm -r "$dir"
```


### Describe the results you received

The script produces unstable image IDs with the Docker API, and stable IDs with the CLI.

The images have different label orders:
```shell
$ for id in 8943fe132a97 8ca0db7b2c69; do podman image history --no-trunc --format '{{.CreatedBy}}' $id | head -1; done
/bin/sh -c #(nop) LABEL "a"="1" "b"="2" "c"="3" "d"="4"
/bin/sh -c #(nop) LABEL "d"="4" "a"="1" "b"="2" "c"="3"
```

### Describe the results you expected

I would have expected stable image IDs in both cases.

comments.body:
Hi, I would like to work on this issue.

From my initial investigation, the possible cause appears to be non-deterministic iteration over a Go map while processing labels in the Docker-compatible build API.

In `pkg/api/handlers/compat/images_build.go`, the JSON labels are unmarshalled into a `map[string]string` and then iterated over to construct the labels slice. Since Go map iteration order is not guaranteed, the generated LABEL instruction order may vary between builds, resulting in different image IDs.

**Proposed approach:**
1. Sort the label keys before constructing the labels slice.
2. Add a regression test to verify deterministic label ordering.
3. Verify that repeated builds through the Docker-compatible API produce identical image IDs.
4. Ensure existing label handling and CLI behavior remain unaffected.

I would be happy to investigate this further and submit a PR. Could you please assign this issue to me?

Since this is the docker API the question is what does docker do firstly, and then we need to match them, if they sort by keys that seems logical to do.

@Prerna2024-cyber see https://github.com/podman-container-tools/community/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md and https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

I am not saying this is not a bug we should fix but the image IDs are no longer guaranteed to be stable in the future as move to other hashes.

From the podman 6 release notes:
 
> In Podman versions 5.x and under, image IDs (for both OCI and Docker v2s2 images) were always equal to the SHA256 digest of the image's config data. A future version of Podman will add support for non-SHA256 digests, and image ID format will change for images that are not using the SHA256 digest. The exact format of the new IDs has not yet been decided, but the assumption that image IDs are valid hashes will no longer be true in future Podman versions.

There is ongoing work where for that, i.e. https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/30246
